questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Under RA 11036, where must a service user's informed consent be recorded?
questions.rationale: Consent, including withdrawal of consent, is recorded in the service user's clinical record.
questions.quote: Such consent shall be recorded in the service user's clinical record

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Within how many hours of admission must a service user be told of their rights under RA 11036?
questions.rationale: Service users must be informed of their rights within 24 hours of admission in a language they understand.
questions.quote: within the twenty-four (24) hours of admission to a mental health facility

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A patient's employer calls asking about his diagnosis. Under RA 11036 the nurse should:
options: Share if the caller is polite
questions.rationale: Records and communications are confidential and may not go to third parties without written consent, except legal exceptions.
questions.quote: shall not be disclosed to third parties without the written consent of the service user

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which situation allows disclosure of a psychiatric patient's records without consent?
options: To stop a threat to another's life
questions.rationale: Exceptions include a court order, a life-threatening emergency to prevent harm, suspected child abuse of a minor, and certain cases against a professional.
questions.quote: A life-threatening emergency exists and such disclosure is necessary to prevent harm or injury

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An adolescent patient reveals signs of child abuse. Under RA 11036, the professional may:
questions.rationale: Disclosure is allowed if the service user is a minor reasonably believed to be a victim of child abuse.
questions.quote: The service user is a minor and the attending mental health professional reasonably believes that the service user is a victim of child abuse

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Under RA 11036, informed consent for treatment, including restraint, must be:
questions.rationale: Service users give written informed consent before any treatment plan, including physical or chemical restraint.
questions.quote: Service users must provide informed consent in writing prior to the implementation

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Under RA 11036, persons with mental health conditions are presumed to:
questions.rationale: All persons, including service users and minors, are presumed to possess legal capacity.
questions.quote: shall be presumed to possess legal capacity

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: During a psychiatric emergency, restraint without consent is allowed only:
questions.rationale: Involuntary treatment or restraint is limited to what is necessary and only while the emergency or loss of capacity persists.
questions.quote: only while a psychiatric or neurologic emergency, or impairment or temporary loss of capacity, exists or persists

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An order for involuntary treatment must be reviewed by the facility's internal review board within:
questions.rationale: The internal review board reviews the order within 15 days of issue and every 15 days while it continues.
questions.quote: within fifteen (15) days from the date such order was issued, and every fifteen (15) days thereafter

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Under RA 11036, disputes on restraint or confinement in a facility are first reviewed by the:
questions.rationale: Facilities must create internal review boards to review cases involving treatment, restraint or confinement.
questions.quote: mandated to create their respective internal review boards

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How is an advance directive made valid under RA 11036?
questions.rationale: A service user states treatment preferences in a signed, dated and notarized advance directive.
questions.quote: through a signed, dated, and notarized advance directive

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which practice violates the rights of service users under RA 11036?
questions.rationale: Users have the right to humane treatment free from solitary confinement and degrading treatment.
questions.quote: Humane treatment free from solitary confinement

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A patient asks to call her sister privately. Under RA 11036 the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Service users may send and receive uncensored private communication and receive visitors at reasonable times.
questions.quote: Send or received uncensored private communication

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: When may a psychiatrist withhold a patient's own clinical record from her?
options: If it would harm her or others
questions.rationale: Access may be withheld if revealing it would harm her health or others' safety; she may contest this with the IRB or CHR.
questions.quote: revealing such information would cause harm to the service user's health or put the safety of others at risk

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Under RA 11036, mental health facilities must keep a register of:
questions.rationale: Facilities maintain a register of all medical treatments and procedures administered to service users.
questions.quote: Maintain a register containing information on all medical treatments and procedures administered to service users

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which act by a nurse is penalized under RA 11036?
questions.rationale: Penalized acts include failing to get consent, violating confidentiality, discrimination and inhumane treatment.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Under RA 11036, who should be trained to deliver mental health services in the barangay?
questions.rationale: DOH and LGUs train BHWs to provide mental health services at the community level.
questions.quote: Capacity Building of Barangay Health Workers (BHWs)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: RA 11036 treats drug dependency primarily as a:
questions.rationale: The Act provides drug screening services consistent with treating drug dependency as a mental health issue.
questions.quote: consistent with the policy of treating drug dependency as a mental health issue
